title: Apptronik Opens Robot Park to Scale Humanoid Data
summary: Apptronik announced on June 30, 2026 the opening of its newly expanded Robot Park, a nearly 90,000-square-foot data collection and training facility for humanoid robots in Austin, Texas, alongside a global network of Robot Park sites at partner and customer locations. Fleets of its Apollo 2 humanoid, offered in both bipedal and wheeled-base configurations, run continuously across these sites performing logistics, manufacturing, and retail tasks to generate teleoperation and autonomous-execution data. That data feeds a research partnership with Google DeepMind to train and refine the Gemini Robotics foundation models, with additional Robot Park deployments running at customer sites including Mercedes-Benz and GXO. Apptronik says the data generated by Apollo 2 today is directly informing its next commercial platform, Apollo 3.
whyItMatters: Robot Park formalizes Apptronik's data strategy: rather than treating humanoid deployment and model training as separate tracks, it turns every fielded Apollo 2 unit into a continuous data-generation node feeding Google DeepMind's Gemini Robotics models. The wheeled-and-bipedal modular split also reflects a practical industry trend, shipping a safety-certified wheeled base for near-term commercial use while the bipedal platform matures in parallel, and the arrangement makes explicit how much of the near-term humanoid roadmap now runs through DeepMind's model work rather than any single hardware maker's own AI stack.
